I expected good service, but what I received was FAR beyond my expectations. This clinic was essential for me to be able to move to Germany with my cats without any problems.

From the beginning, the service was impeccable: they did all the serology, a complete checkup of the animals, and it was during this process that we discovered that my cat needed surgery before the trip. Everything was resolved with professionalism and care.

What impressed me most was the team's dedication: they attended to me at home when I needed them, were with me at the airport on the day of departure, took care of ALL the necessary documentation (and anyone who knows the process of international relocation with pets knows how bureaucratic it is!), and even managed to attend to me on a Saturday, December 27th, which was the only day I had available before the trip.

The team not only did their job - they were partners throughout this entire transition process. They endorsed all the documentation, ensured that every detail was correct, and thanks to that I had NO problems traveling. A special thank you to Dr. Diniz and Rose, who were truly by my side throughout this entire process. Exceptional professionals who make all the difference!

For anyone considering this clinic: you can trust them completely. They are serious, competent professionals who truly care about the well-being of the animals and the peace of mind of their owners. It's worth every penny invested.

My dog ​​started to get more lethargic on Friday, so we scheduled an appointment for Monday morning.
In the afternoon, as recommended by the veterinarian, an ultrasound was done which showed fluid in the lungs, and an X-ray was requested, which we had done that same day.
The result was that the lung was quite compromised and had numerous nodules.
The veterinarian prescribed antibacterial medication and an evaluation for pneumonia (which the clinic only had available in two weeks), without further tests.
We went to another place where they ordered more tests, and the result was cancer, not bacteria or pneumonia.

Edit:
“Unfairly harming in a public way” let's be clear: at no point did I defame the image of your work, but rather recounted my experience as a pet owner.

The evaluation was made based on this real experience, not based on discussions about records, audios, or schedules.

I understand that the report mentioned differential diagnoses, however, from the point of view of someone who had a visibly debilitated dog, with severely compromised lungs and numerous nodules, the course of action taken seemed insufficient given the severity, which was later confirmed by other professionals as advanced cancer.

If the pulmonologist only had availability two weeks later, he could have suggested seeking one outside the clinic, referred me to an oncologist, explored the possibility of the pulmonologist practicing elsewhere, or arranged an emergency appointment.

For me, there is new information, which I consider even worse because if tests were ordered on November 19th by the pulmonologist, they could have been sent immediately given the dog's condition, which did not happen. Saying they didn't send them because they were blocked is not necessarily effective, since the clinic contacted me more than a week later just to ask if I would attend the appointment, and at no point was I asked how the dog or I were doing.

Regarding the initial treatment, I avoided going into detail, but I note that, according to other professionals who followed the case in the following weeks, the prescribed medication would only be compatible with bacterial pneumonia, not considering hypotheses such as pulmonary neoplasia or fungal pneumonia, therefore there is a technical divergence.

What generated my frustration and insecurity was the absence of a more immediate and thorough investigation.

I expected a little more care after seven years of follow-up at the same clinic.

I sincerely hope that other pet owners do not go through the same anguish that I am going through.

I am a foreigner traveling in Brazil and wanted to arrange for the international health certificate for my dog to travel to Uruguay.
Before coming to Vet Pituka I visited another clinic that turned out to be a complete disaster: I ended up loosing my flight and had to start the whole paperwork from the  beginning. This is when Dr. Diniz and Vet Pituka were recommended to me; from the very first minutes I realized that my dog and myself are in good hands — Dr. Diniz is incredibly knowledgeable and took the time to explain everything in detail, answering all of my questions with patience and over the weekend beyond the working hours (an additional plus for me was that Dr. Diniz speaks perfect English and there were no communication issues).
Dr. Diniz and his team clearly cared deeply about my and my dog’s needs and made sure that I have all papers handy and all vaccines are up to date. As a result, I got my dog re-vaccinated and what is more, I received the international health certificate with the stamp from the ministry the same day I visited the clinic — this is an absolutely incredible timeline! I am writing this review from Uruguay and need to emphasize that thanks to Dr. Denis my dog’s check-in at the airport and border control went like a breeze.

I also very much appreciate how thorough Dr. Diniz and his team were with the re-vaccination of my dog. I never felt rushed, and Dr. Diniz went above and beyond to ensure my pet’s well-being. It is evident that this is a team that genuinely loves animals, have great experience, is super knowledgeable and strives to provide the best service possible.

I would highly recommend Vet Pituka to everyone!
